prompt: A T-shape has a $6 \times 2$ top bar and a $4 \times 3$ stem. **Total area**?
hint: A capital T is a bar across the top and a stem below it. Each of those parts is a rectangle.

hints.text: A capital T is a bar across the top and a stem below it. Each of those parts is a rectangle.
The top bar has area $6 \times 2$ and the stem has area $4 \times 3$. Work out both and add them together.
Both parts have area $12$, and $12 + 12 = 24$, so the total area is $24$ square units.

explanation: Split the T-shape into its top bar and its stem, which are both rectangles.
The top bar has an area of $6 \times 2 = 12$ square units.
The stem has an area of $4 \times 3 = 12$ square units as well.
Add the two rectangles: $12 + 12 = 24$, so the total area is $24$ square units.
